series.$note: series.observed holds several sources and must not be read as one curve. DS-35: All greenhouse gases including land-use change, GWP100 (OWID, from Climate Watch / PIK), from 1990. DS-02: Asset-level observed emissions, CO₂e GWP100 (Climate TRACE); land use accounted differently from OWID, 2015-2025. DS-40: Total GHG emissions including LULUCF/LUCF exactly as the Party submitted them to the UNFCCC, on that Party’s own reporting guidelines and GWP set (UNFCCC Data Interface, snapshot of 2024-07-05). Non-Annex I Parties report only the years their national communications cover, and the figure is negative where reported removals exceed reported emissions. Points from an NDC document are that document's own inventory basis. The same year can appear more than once with different values; R3 keeps them side by side and never averages them.

ndc_assessment.vintage: First (I)NDC round, as assessed by WRI CAIT (2016). Not the latest submission.
ndc_assessment.summary: "The Central African Republic aspires to reduce its emissions by 5% and 25%, respectively, in the 2030 and 2050 horizons in comparison to its reference BaU emissions and to increase its sequestration potential. With international support, it will emit around 33,076.1 kt eq-CO 2 less in 2050 than the annual reference emissions. The Central African Republic also aspires to reduce emissions of short-lived climate pollutants (SLCP), which science has shown have a significant short-term climate-warming potential and harmful effects on health, agriculture and ecosystems." The INDC also includes a section on adaptation.
ndc_assessment.ghg_target: 5% reduction by 2030 and 25% by 2050 in GHG emission compared to the reference BAU scenario
ndc_assessment.sectors: Land use, land use change and forestry (LULUCF) (89.46%); energy (5.19%); agriculture (5.26%); waste (0.09%) and industrial processes and use of solvents (2010 data).
ndc_assessment.$note: Third-party assessment of the first (I)NDC round. It is not merged into ndc.*, is not used by derive(), and does not appear on the dial as a target.

evidence.sentence: Sous la configuration du scénario d'atténuation, les émissions atteignent 991 GgCO₂-éq en 2030 et 1 099 GgCO₂-éq en 2035, correspondant à des réductions de 7,8 % et 14 % par rapport au scénario tendanciel.

Dans l'hypothèse d'une mise en œuvre renforcée des mesures dépendantes du financement international, les émissions sont réduites à 919 GgCO₂-éq en 2030 puis 935 GgCO₂-éq en 2035, soit des baisses respectives de 14,4 % et 23,3 % par rapport à la tendance de référence.
Les émissions atteignent environ 4 771GgCO₂-éq en 2035, soit une réduction de près de 14 % par rapport à la tendance de référence.

emissions_profile.$note: Headline totals are OWID only. OWID's CO₂ sub-totals are fossil/industrial CO₂ by fuel, not a full sectoral GHG breakdown, and do not sum to total_mtco2e. DS-05's rows are non-CO₂ gases only and are not comparable with the others; that is also why DS-05 is absent from series.observed, where a shorter curve would read as a disagreement rather than a difference of scope. by_source carries each source whole.

verdict.text: The registry's current submission for this Party is NDC 3.0, filed 2026-03-09. 55 observed values are loaded from DS-02 (11), DS-35 (35), DS-40 (9). For 2024 the sources disagree: DS-35 68.7 MtCO₂e, DS-02 9.1 MtCO₂e. They are on different inventory scopes and the engine does not reconcile them. No implementation gap is reported: 35 observed years are loaded, but no NDC target emissions figure has been parsed, so there is nothing to measure the trend against. It submitted BTR1. 2 of 8 components have been confirmed in the document; the rest are unparsed, which is not a finding against the country. ND-GAIN scores it 27.4 for 2024. In the first NDC round, WRI's CAIT assessment recorded: 5% reduction by 2030 and 25% by 2050 in GHG emission compared to the reference BAU scenario It was classed both. That is a 2016 assessment of an earlier submission, not the target above. Projected warming for 2080-2099 against 1995-2014 ranges from +1.14°C under SSP1-2.6 to +3.86°C under SSP5-8.5. These are model runs, not observations.
